title: Virginia's data centers (clean-energy spot)
claim: "Virginia's data centers are… investing billions in clean energy"; frames data centers as paying their own energy costs
notes: Sponsor spent at least $700K on digital marketing in VA in FY2024. Mailers/fliers also reported.

title: "Businesses are Rethinking Data Centers: Water" / "…: Energy" / "Investing in Energy Projects" / "Building Responsibly"
claim: Video titles only were captured; scripts still need transcribing
notes: 14 videos on the page, embedded without visible YouTube links. Next step: open each one and transcribe its energy and water lines.

title: "Get the facts" ad, Fredericksburg Free Lance-Star
claim: Touts low water use and says data centers are "building responsibly"
evidence: Reported (opinion column; photo of the ad in the article)
notes: A scan of the actual print ad is needed. Free Lance-Star archive or reader submission.

title: Cooling without water spot
claim: Says data centers avoid water for cooling "96% of the time" (per critic's summary)
notes: The blog does not name the specific spot. Low confidence until the video is found.

sponsor: Texas Connects (Data Center Coalition / America Connects)
title: "Data centers: built in Texas. For Texas."
claim: "new technology means data centers consume minimal water while funding new power generation for everyone"
notes: Heatmap reports 12M+ views. The site also has videos titled 'Water', 'Energy' and 'Built Responsibly'.

place: North Carolina (Fox News, Spectrum News Raleigh, radio, billboards)
title: "Committed to paying their costs"
claim: "We pay for every single kilowatt hour"; "committed to paying their costs so North Carolina families don't"
notes: $367,272 spent on 747 spots (The Mountaineer). Ads also address water supply and quality; that wording is not yet captured.

title: "Unlocking a smarter power grid"
claim: "Oregon's data centers are unlocking a smarter power grid for our communities"; "committed to paying their costs, so Oregon families don't"
notes: Group registered Mar 4, 2026, the same day the Oregon House voted on a data center tax-incentive pause.

sponsor: Pennsylvania Connects / Connected Ohio / Indiana Connects / Connected Georgia
title: America Connects state sites
claim: Same template as the other state campaigns; energy and water lines not yet transcribed
notes: Also https://indianaconnects.com/videos/. The home pages make tax and jobs claims but no energy or water claims.

place: Sacramento, Salt Lake City, Tallahassee, Washington DC + other capitals
title: Altoona, Iowa — "we're bringing jobs here"
claim: The spot itself is about jobs; Meta's companion Altoona fact sheet claims 100% renewable energy and water reuse
notes: $6.4M campaign across 8 state capitals + DC (NYT via AdImpact). Kept as campaign context and a comparison case.

title: Los Lunas data center spotlight
claim: Fact sheet: "Meta will be water positive in 2030"; operations "supported by 100% renewable energy"
notes: The spot's own script is not yet transcribed.

title: "Connect us to the entire world"
claim: Connectivity message, reported alongside Meta's campaign
notes: Find the spot and check it for water or energy lines.

title: AWS Virginia Sustainability Fact Sheet; NoVA water claims
claim: Operates "ninety-seven percent of the year by pulling outside air and not using any water"; "dropped water use by 42 percent"
notes: Disputed: a former staffer's lawsuit alleges these claims mislead and that replenishment covers 22–25% of consumption.

title: Community-First AI Infrastructure boards
claim: "We'll pay our way to ensure our datacenters don't increase your…" [electricity prices]; pledge to replenish more water than it uses
notes: The second board set is at …/202603_Boards_Gaines_Charter_Township.pdf. A good poster-format example.

title: Five water commitments for data centers
claim: "Replenish more water than we consume at our sites… by 2030"; $500M for local water projects
notes: This is a PR pledge, not a paid ad. Kept for the 'claims landscape'. Example given: Douglas County, GA wastewater reuse.

sponsor: Build American AI (affiliated with Leading the Future super PAC)
title: Battleground-state data center campaign
claim: Positions data centers as compatible with protecting ratepayers and "water resources"
notes: About $50M cash on hand (Axios). Ad creative not yet captured. Bloomberg and NBC also covered the launch.

title: Delaware data center PR campaign
claim: Says development would keep property taxes low, bring jobs and protect nearby wetlands
notes: Has no direct energy or water claim. The original reporting is by Spotlight Delaware.

title: Husted 'face of data centers' ads
claim: Pledges to "require the data centers pay the full cost of their electricity, not you"
notes: Counter-ad category. $3.5M+ across 3 spots (AdImpact). Over $31M in 2026 political ads mention data centers, more than 99% of it against them.

place: US (Coney Island), UK (London tube), South Korea
title: Anti–data center water ads
claim: Attacks data center water use
notes: Counter-ad category. Placements: King's Cross, Bethnal Green and Hackney stations.

place: National TV (premiered on Kaun Banega Crorepati)
title: "Always Clean, Always On"
claim: "If the future runs on intelligence, intelligence must run on clean power" (chairman); 24×7 clean power for data centres and AI
notes: Agency: Leo India. A child talks with an AI companion. Data centres appear in the imagery. Avaada plans its own green data centres.

title: India South Central cloud region
claim: "Effectively zero water use for cooling"; 1 GW renewable energy contracted in India
notes: Open Magazine notes this is a statement of design intent with no published operating data.

title: Amazon water positive in India
claim: "We do not currently use water for cooling in any of our data centres in India"; returned 120% of water used
notes: Released during the 2026 Mumbai water shortage. Reuters reported scrutiny from Indian authorities.

title: Chennai 1 campus
claim: Powered with "up to 100% renewable energy"
notes: Down To Earth found AdaniConneX does not break out data center water use in its ESG reporting.

title: GreenVolt 1 solar farm
claim: "power 100% of its datacenters with green energy" (future)
notes: The 125 MWp farm covers 60% of the Mumbai campus. CtrlS also markets India's 'only 100% quake & air-pollution-free' data centre.

title: "Excellent Energy efficient awards" (Engineers' Day)
claim: "36% of our power is sourced from zero-carbon renewable sources"
notes: See also the World Environment Day 2023 video: https://www.sttelemediagdc.com/in-en/video/world-environment-day-stt-gdc-india

title: Green Data Centers
claim: "With the lowest PUE and WUE"; 231 MW renewable contracted
notes: The superlative is unqualified. Down To Earth notes Sify claims to save 'billions' of gallons without data.

title: Mumbai 3 (64 MW)
claim: "100% renewable energy"; closed-loop cooling for "near-zero wastewater"; site page: "zero liquid discharge"
notes: Karmactive points out that near-zero wastewater is not zero consumption. No WUE or water source has been published.

title: "India's first carbon-zero data centre"
claim: Aims for "carbon-zero", "not merely carbon-neutral", by 2027–28
notes: Its Chennai facility claims 75% less water use.

title: Joins RE100
claim: Commits to "100% renewable electricity"; net zero by 2031
notes: Pledge, not ad. Kept for the claims landscape.

title: Google AI hub ('AI-patnam')
claim: Gigawatt-scale campus "supported by… clean energy"; new transmission and storage
notes: No specific projects or timelines named (DCD).
